eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: Extensive debate on whether to ship current spec or make changes to mitigate contract breakage before Glamsterdam mainnet.

moments.context: Rahul reported outreach to 50+ companies affected by EIP-8037 repricing, suggesting mid-January as earliest mainnet date since all highs and most mediums said they would be ready by then.

Justin Florentine from Besu argued that breaking try/catch in Solidity via gas accounting changes is more concerning than hard-coded gas pricing breaks, and suggested using the delay time to try to fix the spec.
Lukasz mentioned he proposed spec changes three weeks ago but acknowledged uncertainty about whether full due diligence on alternative breakage was done.
Toni Wahrstaetter cautioned that spec changes could break new invariants and require extensive re-analysis, noting most apps are ready by mid-January.
Dragan Rakita argued there is no silver bullet for two-dimensional gas and the current spec is good enough; any changes would cause delays without protocol-level gains.

Marius van der Wijden explained that the most reasonable spec change—removing in-transaction refunds—would break contracts relying on set-then-clear storage patterns, and drawbacks are not fully understood.
Barnabas pushed to decide today, noting no concrete spec change proposals had been presented after nearly a month. Client team poll showed majority favoring proceeding without changes.
Andrew Ashikhmin from Erigon argued for spending effort on spec changes to preserve smart contract immutability rather than rushing Glamsterdam.

eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Frames transaction EIP discussed as centerpiece of Hegota fork with ongoing spec changes and breakout recap.

moments.context: Ansgar introduced Hegota scope discussion noting frames is already the PQ platform centerpiece; question is whether to reduce scope around it.
Matt gave a frames breakout recap: working on 8288 forward compatibility, considering removing the signature list, and evaluating tree-root-style hashing; spec changes targeted before mid-December.
Nico said in chat that the frames breakout found a way to do PQ multisig with no changes required to Safe or to EIP-8141.

eips.title: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation
eips.summary: In-mempool signature aggregation discussed as future-compatibility target for frames design and potential Hegota addition.

moments.context: Ivan said ethrex would leave an open window for an 8288 forward-compatible solution for PQ signatures enshrined in the protocol.
Matt stated there is no way signature aggregation via 8288 will be in Hegota but frames should be future-compatible with it.
Matt reported the frames breakout is working on becoming more forward-compatible with 8288 by potentially changing or removing the signature list.
Ivan described his draft EIP proposal for minimal leanSPHINCS on top of frames designed to be compatible with 8288 for future aggregation.

eips.title: State-Access Gas Cost Update
eips.summary: Referenced alongside EIP-8037 as part of Glamsterdam repricing that was assessed by auditors.

moments.context: Ivan cited the care being taken with 8037 and 8038 for users as the model for other risky EIPs such as 8151.

eips.title: Account Code Restricted ecRecover
eips.summary: Flagged as needing the same careful user-impact analysis as EIP-8037 due to contracts depending on ecRecover.

moments.context: Ivan flagged that EIP-8151 needs the same care regarding user impact as EIP-8037 and 8038.
Kevaundray reported a preliminary scan showing quite a lot of contracts potentially broken by 8151's ecRecover restriction, raising concern it might not make Hegota.
